- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a mild downward correction (−0.5 to −1.5%).
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5%.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth transitions using 3–5 day moving average of sentiment-weighted price.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.0+ and price is rising, model may overfit to momentum; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid “overbought” bias.
